title: QUIZ - 69
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a mapping diagram represents a valid function
questions.question: Consider the mapping diagram: \( A \to 3, C \to 4, B \to 1, A \to 2 \). Is this a valid function?

options.label: A
options.text: No, because one starting point has two arrows leaving it.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because each starting point has exactly one arrow leaving it.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, because each ending point has exactly one arrow arriving.

options.label: D
options.text: It depends on the direction the arrows are drawn.

questions.explanation: The element A has two outgoing arrows, violating the requirement that each input have only one output.
questions.hint: Check whether any single starting point in the diagram has more than one arrow leaving it.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a set of ordered pairs represents a function
questions.question: Does the mapping {(8, 10), (9, 18), (8, 9), (2, 14)} represent a function?

options.label: A
options.text: Yes, because every input maps to exactly one output.

options.label: B
options.text: It cannot be determined from a list of pairs.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, because every output maps to exactly one input.

options.label: D
options.text: No, because one input maps to more than one output.

questions.explanation: The input 8 appears more than once with different outputs, so this is not a function.
questions.hint: A mapping is a function only if every input is paired with exactly one output.

questions.concept: Definition of a Function as a Mapping
questions.learningObjective: Recall the defining property of a function as a mapping between inputs and outputs
questions.question: Which statement best describes a function as a mapping?

options.label: A
options.text: A rule that assigns multiple outputs to every input.

options.label: B
options.text: A rule that assigns exactly one input to each output.

options.label: C
options.text: A rule that assigns exactly one output to each input.

options.label: D
options.text: Any set of ordered pairs, regardless of repeated inputs.

questions.explanation: By definition, a function maps each input to exactly one output, though different inputs may share the same output.
questions.hint: Focus on what happens to a single input: how many outputs can it have?
